title: Madd and ghunnah in Ya-Sin 33 to 36: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 22 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Madd and ghunnah in Ya-Sin 33 to 36 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 22. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Even counts
points: Muttasil and munfasil: the same 4 or 5

keywords.def: a nasal hum of two counts
a hamza followed by a madd letter: 2 counts
noon becomes a hidden meem before ب

questions.q: Recite 36:34 and mark each ghunnah with a tap.
questions.a: جَنَّٰتٍۢ: نّ; جَنَّٰتٍۢ مِّن: idgham; مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ: idgham; فَجَّرْنَا: no ghunnah (ج shaddah).

questions.q: Ghunnah and madd map (pupil PDF): label every ghunnah and madd in 36:33 to 36. Today's rota group recites 36:29 to 36.
Extend: record 36:33 to 36 (voice only) and check your ghunnah lengths.
questions.a: A short recording uploaded to the portal.

questions.q: Stretch: why does «فَجَّرْنَا» have no ghunnah?
questions.a: The shaddah is on ج, not on ن or م: ghunnah belongs to noon and meem.
A) 2 counts. Ghunnah is held for two counts.

questions.q: Think again: Ya-Sin is often recited aloud by many Muslims. Why does consistent ghunnah and madd make a recitation beautiful?
questions.a: Even lengths give a steady rhythm; the listener can focus on the meaning.
